correctness.rationale: Exact orthonormal coordinates v_{u,a} give every Gabor atom in one rank-m subspace E_a; summing p translation outer products and using injective character labels yields \(S=p^2\sum_a c_aP_a\). This proves all spectra, eigen-atom canonical dual and tightness. Binomial occupancy counting, pigeonhole bounds and equality analysis prove the exact isospectral counts and minimax conditioning for all permitted integers. Direct independent matrix construction passed 1281 spectral/eigenvector tests; 63 exhaustive mask count cases also passed. These are corroborative; proof covers arbitrary parameters.

evidence: Asipchuk–De Carli–Rodriguez: any subgroup translation set gives a block Fourier operator; Corollary 5.1 gives block entries, without a phase-independent eigenvalue distribution for all frequency masks.
The N=12, K={0,3,6,9}, L={0,1,2,3} example from the same paper is tight at eigenvalue 16 and is a strict special case already known.

A related indexed full text: Geometric cyclic Gabor windows: exact translation-mask rank, spectral rigidity, and optimal taper (2026/11/16/92fb6f3665eb), uses geometric positive windows, modulation subgroups and variable q-element translation sets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A generic block-decomposition principle with computable entries does not automatically assert the complete spectral invariant for a special interlaced family, the fact that every atom is an eigenvector, or exact global mask-design enumerations. The acknowledged N=12 example is covered and is not presented as a new contribution. The geometric-window theorem varies the opposite coordinate and uses a different window.

originality.rationale: The full text of Asipchuk–De Carli–Rodriguez (arXiv:2605.16139v2), particularly Theorem 1.1, Corollary 4.3, Corollary 5.1 and the N=12 character-interlace example, was compared statement by statement. It establishes block equivalence and one special tight example but not the complete arbitrary modulation-mask spectrum, phase-independent spectral classes, atom-wise scalar canonical dual and all-cardinality optimal mask census. Other closely indexed one-defect and geometric-window results concern translation-mask problems and do not imply this frequency-mask classification. Derivation from the earlier general block formula remains a meaningful proximity and publication-priority risk, duly acknowledged.
residual_risks: The 2026 general block-equivalence results and their full block-entry formula are close antecedents; the current result is an evaluated structural refinement, not an independent overarching frame principle.
Older equivalent interlaced-character frequency-mask calculations may exist in unindexed literature or under alternate terminology.
Some broad finite-Gabor background sources were assessed from abstracts rather than fully inspected; none was used to prove a novelty-negative claim.

value.rationale: The family is motivated by a recent paper on explicit block-equivalent finite Gabor frames and non-subgroup modulation masks. The exact occupancy-only spectrum, lack of costly dual inversion, full mask classification and exact optimal sampling/erasure counts address the natural design problem of arbitrarily missing frequency labels for this structured window. These are structural spectral and canonical-dual statements, not arbitrary enumerations or unmotivated parameter increments; no claim beyond this restricted finite family.
